name: Every Ample Nonpeelable Family Reduces to a Prime Cornerless Core
statement: Every finite ample non-corner-peelable cube family $X$ reduces to an ample, cornerless, periphery-free, Cartesian-prime, non-corner-peelable family $H$ by repeatedly deleting a corner, replacing a peripheral expansion $(B\times\{0\})\cup(S\times\{1\})$ by a nonempty nonpeelable member of $\{B,S\}$, or replacing a nontrivial Cartesian product by a nonpeelable factor. Every selected intermediate family remains ample and nonpeelable, and the process terminates.
proof: Corner deletion preserves ampleness and nonpeelability: a peeling of the remainder preceded by the deleted corner would peel the original family. Delete corners until the family is cornerless. If a peripheral coordinate remains, the exact expansion test says that at least one nonempty projected section is nonpeelable; select it. If a nontrivial Cartesian factorization remains, the exact product test says that at least one ample factor is nonpeelable; select it. A section or factor selection strictly decreases isometric dimension, while a corner deletion decreases order without increasing dimension. Thus the lexicographically ordered pair (isometric dimension, order) decreases and the process stops at a cornerless family with neither a peripheral coordinate nor a nontrivial Cartesian factor.
comments: In the associated ideal language, the terminal family is a periphery-free Cartesian-prime member of the cornerless linear-ideal class in rank at most that of the input.
